INDEPENDENT ABSTRACT GOOD-CENTER RECTIFIABILITY BASELINE
=======================================================
Authoring status: language-model-assisted internal candidate proof.
Date: 2026-10-09. Worker: complexity_proof_recon, existing Sol/max.
No current broadcasting quantitative proof, or new sibling proof, read.
No harmonic-map representation is an assumption or a derived input here.
Historical priority, external validation, and formal verification: UNKNOWN.

0. Result, distinction from the older dimension theorem
-----------------------------------------------------
The claimed conclusion in this baseline is affirmative: under the exact
measure and frequency conventions below, the full good-center set is
countably (m-1)-rectifiable and has sigma-finite H^(m-1). This is stronger
than a Hausdorff-dimension bound. The proof first obtains finite critical
measure on countably many pieces; it never assumes that finiteness in order
to apply a rectifiability theorem.

The new mechanism is an augmented-center covariance estimate. A center z
is lifted to (2P(z,t),z), so varying frequencies are part of the covariance
rather than an additive error. A uniform SECOND eigenvalue gap for the
integrated PSD block then gives a best-(m-1)-plane estimate linear in the
frequency drop. A maximal-density normalization closes the packing step
using a primary discrete Reifenberg theorem. All centers, including
exceptional centers for arbitrary proposed center measures, are covered by
the same countable decomposition.

The older internally audited abstract dimension proof and previous own
work were available background. No conclusion from that proof is needed
as an axiom below. In particular, global positivity of every ball-height
is not imported: positivity is required only where a good-center frequency
is defined. Radial identities are derived directly from the distributions.

CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE MODULE: DISCRETE DENSITY BOOTSTRAP + AT
Independent reconstruction using named published measure theorems.
This module assumes the UNIVERSAL gamma L2 estimate from CORE_L2_BETA_AND_COERCIVITY.txt; it is not a proof for one preferred center measure.
All gamma choices below use the SAME tuple and SAME frequency P.

There also exist eta_*=eta_*(n,p,N)>0 and A_*=A_*(n,p,N)<infinity
with the following consequence. For R<=1/1024, any Borel S subset Z
such that
  P(z,64R)-P_0(z)<=eta_* for every z in S,
  P_0(z)=lim_{r down to 0}P(z,r),                             (1.4)
satisfies, for every ball B_R(q),
  N_r(S intersect B_R(q))<=A_* (R/r)^k for 0<r<R,             (1.5)
and H^k(S intersect B_R(q))<=A_* R^k, up to the fixed Hausdorff
normalization constant. The same holds on each smaller ball because
the tail in (1.4) decreases when R decreases.

Take R_j=2^{-j}/1024 and
  Z_j={z in Z:P(z,64R_j)-P_0(z)<=eta_*}.                       (1.6)
These Borel sets increase and cover Z. Each has finite H^k measure on
B1, and each is countably k-rectifiable. Thus

  Z has sigma-finite H^{n-1} measure and is countably
  (n-1)-rectifiable.                                        (1.7)

In dimension n=1, Z contains at most one point, so the analogous H^0
and tube conclusions are stronger and need no Reifenberg theorem.
Proof is in section 9.

The theorem does NOT yet assert one uniform critical Minkowski constant
for the whole Z, or local finiteness of H^k on the entire Z. The tail
decomposition can have arbitrarily small starting radii depending on
the tuple. Section 10 gives an additional proved splitting lemma and
the exact remaining framework gate for those stronger assertions.

6. EXACT STANDARD IMPORTS FOR THE CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE

DR: the published discrete Rectifiable-Reifenberg theorem of Naber and
Valtorta, Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), Theorem 3.4. In the version
used here, let disjoint balls B_a(y) lie in B2 and put
gamma=omega_k a^k sum delta_y. There are delta_DR(n)>0,D_DR(n)<infinity
such that the local Carleson condition
  integral_{B_t(q)} integral_0^t beta_gamma,2^k(u,s)^2 ds/s dgamma(u)
                       <=delta_DR^2 t^k
on EVERY interior ball implies gamma(B1)<=D_DR. Scaling is allowed.
The full beta rather than the optional small-mass cutoff is used; this
is a stronger hypothesis and is allowed by the source's Remark 3.2.

REQUIRED APPEND-ONLY SOURCE ALIGNMENT: PUBLISHED DR INNER CENTERS

Status: a literal published-source hypothesis was omitted in the original
DR paraphrase. The proof is repaired by a smaller restriction; no theorem
conclusion, tail threshold, or mathematical constant needs to change.
The original frozen theorem and component files remain byte-identical.
This addendum MUST accompany their use with published NV Theorem 3.4.

1. THE EXACT VERSION DIFFERENCE

The locally pinned arXiv:1504.02043v5 statement of Theorem 3.4, PDF p.24,
allows a collection of disjoint balls lying in B2 and estimates the radii
whose centers lie in B1. The published Annals 185 (2017) statement,
printed p.157 / PDF p.27, also explicitly requires its centers in B1.
The old component names the published theorem but restricts gamma to
B_{3t_i/2}(q'). That restriction satisfies the arXiv statement; it need
not satisfy the additional published inner-center condition after scaling
B_{2t_i}(q') to B2. Thus a literal published-source pass requires repair.

Primary URL:
https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v185-n1-p03-p.pdf
Published PDF SHA256:
8b2bb40b37b7496d55f2f744322fb487979fd22fbd473d3e412c4faaea3a3d61
Local copy: work/agents/cycle10_reifenberg_density_bootstrap_luna/sources/
           naber_valtorta_annals_2017.pdf
ArXiv v5 PDF SHA256:
859bfa4d08c5db95f997b65b16f5c801f1d3536ee4f95469992989b2549c4371

2. REQUIRED REPLACEMENT

At every upward induction step, replace ONLY
  gamma' = gamma restricted to B_{3t_i/2}(q')
by
  gamma' = gamma restricted to the OPEN ball B_{t_i}(q').       (A.1)

Every rescaled center is now in B1, as required by the published theorem.
Every a-ball still lies in B_{2t_i}(q'), since a<=t_i/2 and
|y-q'|<t_i. The original 10a separation makes these balls disjoint.
The scaling gamma_ti=t_i^{-k}(T_ti)#gamma' gives exactly the published
packing measure with weights omega_k(a/t_i)^k. Furthermore,
  gamma'(B_{t_i}(q'))=gamma(B_{t_i}(q')).                      (A.2)
Thus the published conclusion estimates the ENTIRE target inner-ball
mass, not a partial subset of that mass.

All previous weak density bounds for gamma remain valid for gamma'.
The beta inequality is legal for this new gamma' because the SAME P and
the SAME beta constant hold for EVERY finite center measure carried by Z.
